intro.label: The Bedlington Coat
intro.heading: Understanding the Bedlington Terrier Coat
intro.html:
The Bedlington's coat is a distinctive combination of soft and harsh hair — neither purely smooth nor purely curly — that forms a crisp, linty texture when properly maintained. It's one of the lowest-shedding coats among terriers, which makes it a practical choice for owners concerned about pet hair. The characteristic lamb-like silhouette — including the topknot, tasseled ears, and shaped body lines — requires professional trimming to maintain. This is not a wash-and-go coat.

Grooming Tools You'll Need

  • Slicker brush — for daily and weekly brushing
  • Wide-tooth metal comb — for checking for tangles and mats, especially around the ears
  • Grooming scissors (if trimming between professional appointments)
  • Dog-safe shampoo formulated for curly or mixed coats
  • Ear cleaning solution and cotton balls

Finding the Right Groomer

The Bedlington's breed-specific trim pattern is not common knowledge among general groomers. Before booking, ask the groomer if they have experience with Bedlington trims. Show them reference photos. A groomer who trims a Bedlington like a generic terrier will shear off the topknot and lose the breed's distinctive profile. It's worth seeking out someone who knows the breed.

care.label: Regular Routine
care.heading: Weekly and Monthly Grooming Routine
care.html:
2–3 Times Per Week

  • Brush through the coat with a slicker brush — work section by section from neck to tail
  • Follow with a metal comb, particularly around the ears and face where mats form most easily
  • Check the tassels on the ears for debris or matting — these areas tangle faster than the body coat

Monthly

  • Bathe every 4–6 weeks or when dirty. The linty coat texture can trap dirt and odor more than a smooth coat
  • Dry thoroughly — the dense coat holds moisture
  • Trim nails monthly — Bedlingtons are active and their nails wear naturally if walked on hard surfaces, but check monthly
  • Clean ears — the drop ears reduce airflow; check for odor, discharge, or redness

Professional Grooming: Every 6–8 Weeks

The full Bedlington breed trim — shaping the topknot, thinning the ears, tidying the face, shaping the body — requires professional attention every 6–8 weeks. Budget for this as a fixed ongoing cost. Between appointments, the coat can be kept tidy with scissor work around the face and paws, but the full shaping requires skill and the right tools.

special.label: Ear and Skin Care
special.heading: Ear Care and Coat Health
special.html:
The Bedlington's ear structure — drop ears covered in fine, tasseled hair — creates a warm, low-airflow environment that can accumulate moisture and debris. Check ears weekly for odor, redness, or excessive wax. Wipe gently with a cotton ball dampened with ear cleaner. Do not probe deeply into the ear canal. If you notice any of the following, see your vet: head shaking, ear scratching, dark discharge, or an unpleasant smell — these indicate infection, not a grooming issue.

Coat Color and Fading

Bedlington coat colors change with age and sun exposure. Blues may fade to a silver-grey; sandies and livers may lighten. This is normal for the breed. UV exposure from sun can accelerate fading in darker-coated dogs, but this is cosmetic, not a health concern.

Coat vs. Skin Irritation

Some Bedlingtons are prone to skin sensitivity. If you notice excessive scratching, redness at the skin level, or dandruff-like flaking that doesn't respond to regular brushing, consult your vet — this may indicate a skin condition rather than a grooming issue. The coat's texture can mask underlying skin problems until they're quite developed, so check the skin level when brushing, not just the surface of the coat.

faq.q: How often does a Bedlington need professional grooming?
faq.a: Every 6–8 weeks. The breed's distinctive shape — including the topknot, shaped body, and tasseled ears — requires professional trimming to maintain. Between appointments, brush 2–3 times per week to prevent matting. Without regular professional grooming, the coat grows out of shape and becomes difficult to manage.

faq.q: Does the Bedlington Terrier coat mat easily?
faq.a: It can, particularly around the ears, neck, and face where the coat is finer and more prone to tangling. Regular brushing with a slicker brush followed by a metal comb catches developing mats before they tighten. The ear tassels are particularly prone to tangling and should be checked every brushing session.

faq.q: Can I groom my Bedlington at home?
faq.a: You can handle the routine brushing and ear/nail maintenance at home, but the full breed-pattern trim — the topknot, face shape, body lines — requires skill and experience with the breed's specific style. Most owners do home maintenance between professional appointments every 6–8 weeks. If you want to learn the full trim, ask a professional groomer to teach you — it's learnable but takes practice.
